headline: Pretrained biological language models are steered via recurrence, priors, activation edits and RL
label: Steering Biomolecular Language Models
summary: Recent work controls pretrained sequence models with soft beliefs, MSA tuning and RL, while benchmarks and enzyme results show gains are uneven.
synthesis: The dominant thread is control of pretrained biological models through mechanisms external to the base weights. PredMem carries soft logit beliefs across masked co-generation steps without training. ARCADE uses activation engineering to steer CAI, minimum free energy and GC content. CPPainter pairs a protein language model classifier with an RL-guided masked-LM generator, and MANTA uses language-model priors to condition IDP ensemble generation. A further preprint treats MSA content as a tunable input for generation and folding. Evidence on transfer is cautionary: MLDEx benchmarks 557,143 simulated directed-evolution campaigns across 16 landscapes, and MSA Transformer features give mixed gains for enzyme recommendation. New relative to earlier benchmark-centered work is the focus on steering inputs, states and objectives during generation.
